title: Naturality of canonical derived base change in its coefficient
statement: Fix derived categories of modules for all schemes [def-pc-derived-category], a commutative square g′:X′→X, f′:X′→S′, f:X→S, g:S′→S with g′;f=f′;g [def-pc-scheme], and k:K→L in D(O_X). The canonical base-change maps [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] satisfy (Rf_*;Lg*)(k);BC_f(L)=BC_f(K);Rf′_*(Lg′*(k)) [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-derived-pullback]. No cartesian or geometric finiteness hypotheses are needed.

proof.text: For L⊣R, L′⊣R′, P,Q and e:P;L′≅L;Q, move P(R(k)) and R′(Q(k)) through the Hom equivalence by its left and right naturality. Naturality of e at R(k) and then naturality of the counit give equal transposes. This is the private mate_naturality lemma.

Use the exact pinned composition comparison c(f′,g);eqToIso(h inverse);c(g′,f) inverse and the canonical pullback adjunctions in the definition of schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap. Expand only the displayed comparison components and functor composition. The preceding mate identity is exactly the coefficient naturality equation.

lean.statement:
theorem schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap_naturality
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (h : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g) {K L : schemeDerivedCategory X} (k : K ⟶ L) :
    (schemeDerivedDirectImage f ⋙ derivedPullback g).map k ≫
        schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' h L =
      schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f f' g g' h K ≫
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage f').map ((derivedPullback g').map k)
